uncited: This family addresses the excessive memory footprint and computational cost of standard Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) by reducing model size through low-rank approximations, tensor decompositions, and pruning.

It differs from sibling methods that modify architecture for specific tasks (e.g., [Binary Radiance Fields](13622-binary-radiance-fields.md) or [Mip-NeRF 360 MLP Architecture](14098-mip-nerf-360-mlp-architecture.md)) by focusing strictly on compressing the existing radiance field representation while preserving rendering quality.
The core mechanism involves approximating high-dimensional parameters (typically fully connected layer weights in the MLP renderer or the radiance field tensor itself) using low-rank structures.
This reduces the number of trainable parameters from $O(N^2)$ or $O(N^3)$ to $O(N \cdot r)$ or $O(N \cdot r^2)$, where $r$ is the target rank.
The motivation for compression arises from the quadratic or cubic scaling of NeRF parameters with respect to network depth and width.
Early works like NSVF [MST*21] and TensoRF [CLBL22] explored hybrid tensor-MLP approaches.
